raw_plan.interpretation: One acquisition email for a solution-aware planner or diary shopper, introducing Papier through its documented academic-year diary rather than assuming the reader is already a customer. The email will invite the reader to explore the academic-year diary guide before deciding whether the August-to-July format suits them.

intent.desired_action: Explore Papier's academic-year diary format and decide whether its built-in planning structure suits the reader's year.

raw_plan.reader: A planner or diary shopper considering how to organise an academic year and comparing available diary formats.
raw_plan.reader_scope: Solution-aware shoppers considering an August-to-July academic-year diary. Do not assume they are students, have missed deadlines, currently use another planner, or have previously bought from Papier.
raw_plan.promise: Papier offers an academic-year diary that brings weekly and term-level planning, deadline and grade tracking, and reflective space into one paper diary.
raw_plan.orientation: Papier's academic-year diary is an August-to-July paper planner with weekly overviews, monthly spreads, term timetables, deadline and grade trackers, and space for goals and reflection.
raw_plan.arc: In this single email, move the reader from recognising Papier as a stationery brand to seeing one concrete reason to explore it: an academic-year diary designed around both the practical and personal shape of the year.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: A single acquisition email should lead with the strongest documented match to the reader's planning job: the diary's built-in weekly, monthly and term structure. The CTA goes to the official guide that explains this mechanism, allowing an unknown reader to assess the format without assuming purchase readiness. Personalisation is retained as a complete alternative proposition rather than diluting the primary argument.

emails.selection_reason: The built-in academic-year structure directly supports the selected audience's job of organising deadlines, terms and personal plans in one diary, and the official guide gives them a low-friction way to explore whether that format suits them.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the reader plans around an academic calendar, they can keep weekly priorities, term dates, deadlines, grades, goals and reflections within one year-shaped paper diary.
value_case.mechanism: The diary runs from August to July and combines weekly overviews and monthly spreads with term timetables, deadline and grade trackers, and dedicated space for goals, notes, gratitude and reflection.
decision_conditions: The documented format is an academic-year diary running from August through July; suitability for a calendar-year planning cycle is not established by this proposition.

claim_conditions: Keep all capability claims specific to Papier's academic-year diary.
Present the organisational benefit as a useful possibility, not a guaranteed customer result.
emails.target_audience: Planner or diary shoppers considering an academic-year format for organising their year.
emails.job: Give the reader a concrete reason to explore Papier and prompt them to consider whether its August-to-July diary structure fits how they plan.
emails.single_idea: Papier's academic-year diary gives the year a visible structure, bringing weekly and monthly planning, term timetables, deadline and grade tracking, and reflective space into one place.
emails.status_quo: Shoppers may be weighing academic-year, mid-year and calendar-year diary formats before choosing one.
emails.mechanism: Show how the August-to-July format is built around the academic calendar, then make the value tangible through its weekly overviews, monthly spreads, term timetables, trackers and reflective sections.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: Personalisation offers a distinct, supported reason to explore Papier for shoppers who want a diary that feels specifically theirs rather than generic.

value_case.reader_benefit: The reader can make an academic-year diary recognisably their own by putting their name and an optional personal title—such as their degree—on it.
value_case.mechanism: Papier applies the buyer's chosen name and optional custom diary title during the purchase flow.
decision_conditions: This personalisation is documented for Papier's academic-year diaries.
The evidence does not establish support for special characters, non-standard spellings or every culturally diverse name.

claim_conditions: Limit the proposition to documented name and diary-title personalisation.
Do not claim that every name, alphabet or special character can be rendered accurately.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: A Papier academic-year diary can carry both the reader's name and a title of their choosing, turning a practical planner into something visibly personal.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: During the purchase flow, the buyer chooses their name and may also choose the diary title itself, such as a degree name or another personal phrase.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: a personalised diary means little more than adding a standard name to a cover. After: Papier lets the buyer shape both the name and the diary title, within the documented academic-year range.
must_not_say: Do not claim accurate rendering of special characters, non-standard spellings, culturally diverse names or every alphabet.
Do not claim Papier is the only stationery brand offering personalisation or make an unverified competitor comparison.
Do not imply that the guide displays current inventory, pricing or every available personalisation option.
alternative_arguments.objection: Will the personalisation be meaningful enough to make the diary feel like mine?
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether name-and-title personalisation makes Papier's academic-year diary appealing enough to consider.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The guide explains that Papier's academic-year diaries can be personalised with both a name and a chosen diary title.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The guide does not establish support for every spelling, character set or current design option.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Earn the open with the specific possibility of putting more than a name on an academic-year diary; avoid generic claims about personalised stationery.

events.subject: Give your academic year shape
events.preview_text: Bring term dates, weekly priorities and reflection into one August-to-July diary.
events.body:
Map term dates across the months, set weekly priorities and keep deadlines visible — with room for the goals and reflections that give the year its shape.

Papier’s academic-year diary is a paper diary running from August to July. Weekly overviews, monthly spreads and term timetables bring plans together, while deadline and grade trackers give key details a dedicated place.

There’s space for notes, gratitude and personal reflection too, so practical plans and personal moments can live within the same year-shaped pages.

Our guide explains the academic-year format and walks through the diary’s planning sections, helping you decide whether its August-to-July rhythm suits the way you organise your year.

events.preview_text: Explore two layouts, two bindings and the planning sections inside.
events.body:
Papier’s academic-year diary runs from August through July, with a week-to-view or day-to-view layout. It gives the academic calendar a paper home you can make your own.

Choose a hardback designed to fit comfortably into most bags, or a larger spiral with more room to write. Add your name and, if you like, a custom diary title.

Inside, weekly overviews, monthly spreads and term timetables sit alongside deadline and grade trackers, with dedicated space for goals, notes, gratitude and reflection. Practical plans and personal pages stay together across the same academic year.

The Papier guide explains the August-to-July format and its planning sections, so you can decide whether that rhythm belongs on your desk.
